references_json: ["People have different dreams when they sleep. Some common dreams are flying, falling, losing teeth, or being outside with no clothes. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people. To know what your dream means, think about what is happening in your life and how you feel.", "Dreams can tell us something about our thoughts and feelings, even if we don't realise it. Many people have similar dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being in public without clothes. These dreams often have the same meaning for most people. To really understand your dream, you should think about your daily life and emotions."]

["There are many wild dogs in Moscow, about 35,000. Some were born wild, and some were pets but left by their owners. Some live alone and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs. They found that the dogs have learned how to live in the city. Some dogs wait and cross the street with people. A few dogs even seem to know traffic lights.", "One interesting example of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs in Moscow. There are around 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of them were born in the wild, and others were once pets but were left by their owners. Some dogs live alone, and some stay in groups. In 2010, scientists studied them and found that the dogs have learned to live well in the city. They often cross the street with people, and some even seem to understand traffic lights."]

["Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio, a writer from New York. She got the idea after seeing a girl with a face that looked different. The book is very popular in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools use the book to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is now being made, and many people want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.", "Wonder is the first novel by RJ Palacio, who comes from New York. She says that she got the idea for the story after seeing a girl with a facial difference on the street. The book became a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools use it to start conversations about bullying, friendship, and how it feels to be different. A film version is now in progress, and many people are excited to read her next book."]

["Chloe has two pet rats, called Zena and Roxy. She knows that rats are not usual pets, and many people think they are dirty. Chloe often tells people that rats can be very good pets if you take care of them. She didn't like rats before, but her friend Martin showed her his rats. She saw they were kind and clever. Last year, one of Martin's rats had babies. Chloe chose two of them to keep.", "Chloe owns two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows rats are not common pets, and she has tried many times to explain that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if you care for them properly. She understands why people are unsure about rats: she didn't like them either until her friend Martin showed her his. After seeing how loving and smart they were, she changed her mind. When one of Martin's rats had babies last year, Chloe decided to keep two of them."]

["Cape Town can be dangerous for baboons. Some are hurt or die in car accidents. Some die from playing with electric wires. Baboons are animals that are in danger of disappearing. To help them, the city now has a team called Baboon Monitors. These people try to move baboons out of the city and take them back to the countryside. This plan works a little, but the baboons often come back because they find food in the city.", "Cape Town is a risky place for baboons. Some are injured or killed by cars, and others are electrocuted when they touch electric wires. Because baboons are an endangered species, the city has hired a group called Baboon Monitors. Their job is to keep baboons out of the city by chasing them away or catching them and releasing them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it's difficult to stop the baboons from returning since they see the city as a place to find easy food."]

["I work for a large IT company, but I work from home because the office is in the USA. I do everything online. This is good because I don't waste time going to work or talking too much with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this is helpful. I can take time off if my children have a school show or if I need to see the dentist. But there is a problem: I don't have fixed hours, so I often work late and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.", "I work for a global IT company, but since the main office is in the United States, I do all of my work from home online. This is helpful because I save time: no travel and no small talk with coworkers. I work on different projects, and I really like the flexibility. I can take time off if my children have something at school or if I need to go to the dentist. However, there is a disadvantage. Without clear office hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes miss dinner just to finish a task."]

["In the 1990s, street art became more popular. Some artists wanted to show ideas about war, unfair treatment, and other problems. Other artists only wanted to make the streets look beautiful. In South America, many artists painted in poor areas. Their art added colour and life to the grey walls.", "During the 1990s, graffiti continued, but street art also became much more popular around the world. Some artists used street art to talk about politics and serious issues like war, inequality, and discrimination. Others focused on making beautiful and interesting art. In South America, many street artists painted in poor neighbourhoods to bring colour and beauty to the grey walls of the cities."]

["Every day, people see many clothes and shoes on social media, in magazines, and in shops. In the UK, people are buying more than before. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking. Big brands sell clothes that are very cheap. Some people wear them only a few times and then throw them away.", "Social media, magazines, and shop windows show people many things to buy every day. In the UK, people are now buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it quick and easy to buy things, sometimes without thinking. Big brands often sell very cheap clothes, so many people wear them only two or three times and then throw them away like rubbish."]

["Sam looked at a car coming to the Big House. The car made a lot of dust. The horses moved their tails to stop the flies. They didn't care that their owner was coming after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter came only when he had to, and Sam liked that. If he stayed away from his boss, he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped his neck. His shirt was wet from sweat. His skin was red from the hot June sun. Normally, he stayed inside and made money while others worked.", "Sam narrowed his eyes at the dust in the distance. A car was coming up to the Big House. The horses kicked and moved their tails to stop the flies, not caring that their owner hadn't visited for ten months. Sam stood and waited. Mr. Carter only came when necessary, and Sam was happy about that. The less he saw his boss, the safer his job was. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. His shirt had wet spots, and his skin was getting red from the summer sun. Normally, he stayed indoors, making money while others did the hard work."]

["In Berlin, Germany, many people were upset because hunters were killing pigs. They thought it was too cruel. The city listened and changed the plan. Now people cannot feed pigs, and fences have been built. This is a kinder way to stop pigs. But there are still many pigs, because the winters are getting warmer.", "In Berlin, Germany, many local people complained that shooting pigs was too cruel. This caused strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Because of the protests, the city council chose a more peaceful solution. They put up fences and made it against the law to feed wild pigs. It's not clear if the plan will work, since warmer winters have caused the number of pigs to grow more than before."]

["The writer of The Hunger Games, Suzanne, got the idea from old Greek stories. When she was young, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, the city of Athens must send children to a monster called the Minotaur every year. The Minotaur lives in a maze and eats the children. One boy, Theseus, fights the monster and kills it. Suzanne thinks Katniss, the main character in The Hunger Games, is like Theseus, but in the future.", "One big inspiration for The Hunger Games came from Suzanne Collins' love of ancient Greek myths. As a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, Athens is controlled by Crete, and every year the king of Crete, Minos, makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls. These children are sent into a maze where a monster, the Minotaur, lives. Theseus, one of the children, kills the monster. Suzanne sees her character Katniss as a modern version of Theseus."]

["Zoos bring people and animals together. They help people learn how to protect animals and nature. Some zoos give homes to animals that were hurt in circuses or left by their owners. Zoos also study animal behavior and how to help sick animals.", "Zoos connect people with animals and help teach the public about protecting animals and the environment. Some zoos give a safe home to animals that were treated badly in circuses or pets that were abandoned. Zoos also do important research on animal behaviour and how to treat their illnesses."]

["Some people are starting a new idea called the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the 1990s and then went to the USA. These people don't like buying too much on days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest and cut their credit cards. During the year, they also fix and trade things instead of buying new ones.", "A new movement against consumerism is growing – it's called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US. People involved in this movement want to avoid overspending, especially during shopping events like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, they hold protests and even cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, they also organise activities to repair or exchange used items instead of buying new ones."]

["Some people think graffiti is art. Others think it is bad. In many countries, painting on public or private places is not allowed. The police often stop street artists, and some must pay fines. Many cities say that cleaning graffiti from buildings and buses costs a lot of money.", "Some people see graffiti as art, while others think it is vandalism. In many countries, painting or writing on public or private property is against the law. Street artists are often stopped by the police, and some are fined. City councils often complain about how expensive it is to clean graffiti from walls, buses, and trains."]

["What do people in the art world think about street art and graffiti? Today, more people see it as a true kind of art. Big art shows in Paris, London, and Los Angeles have shown street art. In 2008, an American artist, Elura Emerald, made a street art show in New York. She said street artists only want to share their ideas and are not doing anything wrong.", "How does the art world view graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as a real form of art. Large exhibitions featuring street art have been held in cities like Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists, saying they are simply expressing themselves and not doing harm, and that they should be respected and celebrated."]

["Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they turn 10. That means around 2,000 dreams every year. By age 80, a person may have about 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95?C99% of our dreams, we still remember many. So, it's not strange if something we dream later happens in real life, especially if it is something we often see in daily life.", "After the age of ten, most people have between four and six dreams each night. That adds up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the time someone turns 80, they may have had around 140,000 dreams. Even though we forget most dreams–about 95 to 99 percent–we still remember thousands over a lifetime. So, it's not hard to believe that sometimes a dream is followed by a real-life event that feels similar, especially when it's about something that happens often in everyday life."]

["The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America is gone. The new country is called Panem. It has 12 poor districts and one rich city, the Capitol. The Capitol has full power. Each district makes something for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives coal. There was a District 13, but it fought against the Capitol and was destroyed.", "The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America has been destroyed. The new country is called Panem, which includes twelve poor districts ruled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol controls the entire country. Each district has its own job and sends goods to the Capitol. The story begins in District 12, which produces coal. There used to be a District 13, but it rebelled and was later destroyed by the Capitol."]

["Wild animals often go into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now go into areas near people's homes. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens. Some baboons are very brave and go into houses to take food from kitchens. Baboons can be dangerous and sometimes hurt pet animals. Many people in the city do not want them around.", "Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun coming into areas where people live. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some even go into homes and take food from kitchen cupboards and fridges. Since baboons can be aggressive and have attacked many pets, it's easy to understand why many city residents don't want them nearby."]

["Many accidents with bridges happen while they are being built. These accidents often happen because engineers make mistakes, like wrong numbers. The bridge can fall down from its own weight. This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge.", "Many bridge accidents happen during construction. These are often caused by mistakes made by engineers, such as wrong calculations. When this happens, the bridge may collapse under its own weight, which can be deadly for the workers on it at the time."]

["George Lucas was one of the first movie makers to use 'the hero's journey' idea. In this story, the hero starts with a normal life. Then something happens that begins an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke lives with his aunt and uncle and fixes robots. One day, he finds a message from Princess Leia. This is the start of his journey.", "George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base a story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. In this type of story, the hero begins with a normal life, but something happens that sends them on an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke Skywalker lives with his aunt and uncle and works on robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message in the robot R2D2, it becomes his 'call to adventure' and marks the beginning of his journey."]

["One way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to break it with a strong bomb, which is nuclear weapon. This may sound like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon. But NASA had a real plan on this. The plan was to send big rockets, about eight tons, to hit the asteroid and push it away. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rocket would take the nuclear bomb to blow it up.", "Another way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to destroy it with a nuclear weapon. This may sound like a film story, and it was actually in the 1998 film Armageddon. However, the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real project from NASA. The plan was to send eight-ton heavy rockets towards an asteroid to push it away from its path. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rockets could carry nuclear bombs to break it apart."]

["Campbell says that first, the hero does not want to go on the adventure. Then a teacher, also a mentor, comes to help. The hero then goes into a \"special world\" where the adventure happens. In this world, the hero has to do tests, fight enemies, and meet new friends before the biggest fight. Luke's teacher is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader inside the Death Star.", "According to Campbell, the hero first refuses to start the adventure. Then a mentor appears and helps them, so the hero decides to \"cross the threshold\" and enter the \"special world\" where the adventure takes place. In this world, Luke's mentor is Obi-Wan,  his friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader in this special world of the Death Star."]

["Things that we don't use much may look useless, but other people may need them. With the internet, people have found a way to share these things and make money. Website and social media groups now help people to buy and sell used goods. It is easy for people to share with each other in this way. This is the sharing economy.", "Some things that are not often used may look useless to people, but they can be valuable to others. With the internet, online groups have found a way to make money by sharing unused items. With websites and social media pages that help people buy and sell second-hand goods, it is now easier for people to share items with each other. This is called the sharing economy."]

["In the 18th and 19th centuries, people had two main ideas about dreams. The first idea was that dreams show things that we dont know in our mind. Freud believed that if we look at dreams, we can understand our hidden feelings and problems. The second idea was opposite. It said dreams are only random things in the brain when it is cleaning and organising the day's memories. When we wake up, we try to make a story from these pics and feelings.", "In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. The first was that dreams show things that are hidden in our minds. Freud thought that by studying dreams, we can learn about our secret feelings and the problems they create. The second idea was the opposite. It said that the dreams are the result of random brain activity while it is sorting memories and events from the day. When we wake up, our brain tries to connect these random images and feelings into a story."]

["I am a freelancer, so I work for myself. This is good as I can choose what to do and how to spend my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus. There were many things around me, like housework, making tea and families asking for attention. Then I tried to work in a cafe, but the internet was not good and I drank too much coffee. In the end, I rented a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancer. I liked dressing up for the office and going to work in the morning.", "I work as a freelancer, which means I work for myself. I like it because I can decide what to do and how to use my time. At first, I worked from home, but I had trouble concentrating. There were many distractions, such as doing household, making tea, and family members wanted me to listen to them. Then I tried to working in a cafe, but the wifi was not very good and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I chose to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed dressing for work in the morning and focusing better in an office environment."]

["NASA needs money to build NEOCam, a space telescope with a small lens, to find the rest of the middle-sized asteriods. This telescope would use infrared light to look for them. If NASA gets the money, it could finish this in 10 years. After that, the team must still plan how to stop the very dangerous asteriods, called PHAs, from hitting Earth.", "NASA can only find the rest of the middle-sized asteriods if it gets money to build NEOCam, a space telescope with a 0.5-meter lens that uses infrared light to find them. With enough money, NEOCam could probably finish this work in 10 years. But after that, the planetary defence team would still have to think about how to protect Earth from the most dangerous asteroids, called PHAs."]

["The \"buy nothing\" idea is now gaining popularity among social media influencers. Normally, they show clothes and make-up for people to buy. But now, some YouTubers tell their fans not to buy anything, even for one year. Two friends in Canada did this and only bought food for a year. In the first three months, they stopped buying electronics, clothes, and things for the house. Later, they also stopped paying for services, like haircuts, eating in restaurants, and petrol for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.", "The \"buy nothing\" concept has now become popular among influencers on social media, who normally post about clothes and make-up for people to buy. Some YouTubers now ask their followers to stop shopping completely, even for a year. In Canada, two friends tried this challenge and only bought food. In the first three months, they learned to live without buying things like electronics, clothes, or things for the house. Later, they also gave up services such as haircuts, eating in restaurants, or paying for petrol for their cars. In one year, they had saved $55,000"]

["Religion is important for Pi. His family is Hindu, but he is also interested in other religions. He makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. One day, Pi says that he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. His family and teachers ask him to choose only one religion, but Pi says, \"I just want to love God.\" After this, his family and teachers let him choose his way.", "Religion is very important to Pi. His family is Hindu, but he is also interested in other religions. He becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says that he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers tell him to choose only one religion, Pi refuses and says, \"I just want to love God.\" After that, his family and teachers allow him to decide for himself about religion."]

["Some people think that writing down dreams in a notebook can help them have lucid dreams. A lucid dream is when you know you are dreaming, and you can change what happens. For example, you can make a bad dream feel safe, or you can control the story like a movie director. In this way, you are not only looking for the meaning of your dreams, but also making them. But sometimes, you may still want dreams that show what is in your mind.", "Some people think that writing down their dreams can help them experience lucis dreaming. A lucid dream is a dream where you know you are dreaming and can make choices that change what happens. For instance,  you might turn a nightmare into a dream that feels safe, or you could guide the story of the dream like a film director. This means you are not only trying to understand your dreams but also creating them. Still, you may want to keep some dreams that show what your subconscious mind is thinking."]

["Some people don't know they are part of the clothing waste problem because they give old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all of them. Fast fashion quickly goes out of style and is often poor in quality, so people don't want to buy second-hand. A lot of clothes are thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries. This causes money and environmental problems.", "People don't realise they are part of the problem of disposable clothing because they give their unwanted clothes to charity shops. However, these shops cannot sell everything. Fast fashion quickly goes out of style and is often too low in quality to recycle, so people don't want to buy it second-hand. As a result, a large amount of clothes are thrown away, and many that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, which creates more economic and environmental problems."]

["Some adventurers today like to do many difficult trips. Meagan McGrath from Canada climbed the tallest mountain on each continent, rode her bike across Canada, and ran a long race in the Sahara Desert, where it was 45ºC. But maybe her most special trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help to get out. Many people would stop there, but Meagan continued. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sledge with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.", "Some modern adventurers do not stop after one amazing trip but keep looking for new challenges. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the tallest mountain on each continent, cycled across Canada, and run a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in 45ºC heat. However, the most impressive journey may have been skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. Many people would have quit, but Meagan continued. Forty days later, she reached the South Pole after pulling a sledge with her tent and food through weather and ice storms."]

["Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls of Paris, his home city. Now, he uses his art to talk about social problems. In big cities, he paints pictures of homeless people to make others think about homelessness.", "Blek le Rat was known for painting rats on the walls of Paris, his home city. Nowadays, his art focuses on social issues and problems. For example, he paints images of homeless people in big cities to make residents think more about the issue of homelessness."]

["In some places, councils want artists to stop painting graffiti anywhere on the walls. Instead, they give them special places to paint. In Taiwan, there are \"graffiti zones\" where artists can paint and write on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the council also lets some graffiti artists paint on the city's subway trains.", "In some places, local councils try to stop random graffiti by giving artists special areas to paint. Taiwan  has \"graffiti zones\" where artists can freely paint and write on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city council has even allowed some graffiti artists to paint on the subway trains."]

["Faith47 comes from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals. She likes to paint in many places, like on pavements, in empty factories, and on old cars. And we can see her work in these places. She enjoys that street art does not last forever and will be removed by rain or by city cleaners. For her, this shows that life is always changing, with things ending and new beginnings.", "Faith47 is an artist from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints big, colourful images of people and animals and enjoys working in many different places. Her art can be seen on pavements, in empty factories, and on abandoned cars. She likes that most street art is temporary and will eventually disappear because of the weather or city cleaners. For her, this shows that life is always changing, with endings and new beginnings."]

["In her old job, Gabriela worked in a place with high power distance. This means people respect authority, and leaders make the big decisions. Workers do not usually question their bosses. But her Swedish team worked in a low power distance culture. Here, workers and bosses make decisions together. Leaders act like coaches or teachers, and they want workers to think for themselves and even question them.", "In her old job, Gabriela worked in a culture with high power distance. In this culture, people respect power and authority, and everyone has a clear place. Leaders make the big decisions, and others do not usually question them. But her Swedish team was used to a low power distance culture. In this culture, employees often work with their bosses to solve problems and make decisions together. Leaders act more like coaches or mentors, encouraging independent thinking and expecting to be challenged."]

["When Gabriela saw that she and her team had cultural differences, she chose to talk with them openly about her leadership. The team was glad to be asked and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom and space to be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their job. They also saw that Gabriela felt upset when they questioned her decisions. They explained that this was just the way they normally worked.", "When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences between her and her team, she decided to have an open conversation with them about her leadership. The team was happy to share their thoughts and explained that they were not used to being told exactly what to do. They enjoyed having more space for initiative and creativity. When Gabriela gave them strict instructions, they felt she did not trust them to do their jobs well. They also realised that Gabriela was taking it personally when they challenged her decisions. They explained that this was the normal way they worked."]

They create street art ranging from small tags to large, colourful paintings of people on building walls. Their work are often so big that they need cranes to help them. ["People have painted and written on walls for a very long time. In early times, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people inside caves. Graffiti has also been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many graffiti messages in Latin. These messages were about religion, politics, love, and even magic spells!", "People have painted and written on walls in history. In prehistory, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people on the walls of caves. Graffiti has also been found on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti in Latin. These messages included religious, political, and romantic topics, and even some magic spells!"]

["Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or going to the South Pole? Many people have. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. In the past, explorers used maps and compasses, but now they use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and want to tell people about environmental problems. Others want to help people in need and collect money for charities.", "Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? You are not the only one. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the world's highest mountains or cross continents on foot. Unlike the explorers in the past, who only had maps and compasses,  today's adventurers use modern technology such as GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature adn use their journeys to raise awareness about environmental issues. Others travel to raise money for charities and to help people in need."]

["The first project is DART- the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. It will be tested on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. This moon is called \"Didymoon.\" It is 150 metres wide and goes around its bigger \"mother\" asteroid, which is 800 metres wide. Scientists hope that when DART hits Didymoon, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.", "The first project is called DART-the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. Scientists plan to test it on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. This moon, called \"Didymoon,\" is 150 metres wide and goes around its larger parent asteroid, which is 800 metres wide. The hope is that the impact of DART will move Didymoon slightly out of its orbit so that telescopes on Earth can detect the change."]

Katniss is very good at shooting with a bow and arrow. One day, her sister Prim is chosen to fight in the Games. Katniss says she will go instead. The other tribute is a boy called Peeta, and Katniss has a strange and hard relationship with him.", "The heroine of the story, Katniss Everdeen, is a sixteen-year-old girl and her father died in a mining accident. When her little sister Prim is chosen to fight as a tribute, Katniss offers to go instead. The boy tribute from District 12 is Peeta, and Katniss soon has a confusing relationship with him."]

After one week, you will see that you have written a lot. ["In the past, many bridges were made of wood. Wood can burn easily. Train bridges had a big problem, because the steel wheels on the steel tracks made sparks. The sparks could make the wooden bridge burn.", "In the past, many bridges were built from wood, which made them easier to burn. This problem was especially common with old train bridges, because sparks from the steel wheels on the steel tracks could sometimes start a fire and destroy the whole bridge."]

["Society tells us that girls should choose arts and humanities, and boys should choose maths and physics. Another problem is that children do not often see women working in science. There is also a negative idea that scientists are \"geeky,\" have poor social skills, or work alone, far from the real world. These are false stereotypes shown by the media, but they may stop girls from seeing themselves as scientists and make science seem unattractive.
